title: Keypad Conundrum
description: Minimize button presses through a chain of directional keypad robots.
writeup:
## Approach

A chain of robots: the last one types on a numeric keypad, each intermediate one controls the next via a directional keypad. We need the minimum total presses on the first (human-operated) directional pad.

## Key Insight

The problem is recursive: to press a button on robot N's pad, robot N-1 must navigate its directional pad and press A. The cost of each move depends only on the current key, target key, and chain depth — making it perfectly suited for memoised recursion.

For each transition on a keypad, we enumerate all shortest paths (avoiding the gap), and recursively compute the cost of each path at the next level. Memoisation on `(from_key, to_key, depth)` makes this efficient.

## Part 1 & 2

2 intermediate directional robots for part 1, 25 for part 2. The memoised approach handles both instantly.
